rv.q: No wonder playwright Max Posner revels in incongruities in 'Hanukkah Spectacular,' his absorbing, funny and brazenly untidy play about the creation of a brazenly untidy play.
Despite the story strands that never make sense and thanks to the actors, Hanukkah Spectacular is well-assembled theatre.

There is excitement in a new play willing to wrestle with complicated questions, and the cast’s considerable talent keeps the production engaging even when the material gets a little tangled in its own ambitions.
Hanukkah Spectacular might be a play or the disembodied limbs of several, but it certainly isn't finished.

cn.t: Strong performances elevate this uneven dark comedy, but critics find it more puzzling than spectacular—leaving audiences questioning both its humor and its connection to the holiday it's named for.
